preflight.name: agent-preflight
preflight.title: Give agents a checkpoint.
preflight.summary: A small local Python package that validates structured agent actions before execution.
preflight.problem: An agent can propose an action with missing arguments, an invalid type, or a name the workflow should never allow. A checkpoint makes those boundaries explicit before a handler runs.
preflight.decision: Keep the validation layer small, local, and inspectable. Required fields and simple schemas cover a focused use case; JSONL and SQLite audit backends make decisions available for inspection. The execution wrapper defaults to dry-run mode.
preflight.evidence: The repository documents a Python API, CLI, configuration files, schema validation, audit records, and a dry-run execution wrapper.
preflight.limits: Early release. This is not a complete policy engine or a production security boundary. No production adoption or performance claims have been verified for this portfolio.

bogdai.name: BogdAI
bogdai.title: Read between the clauses.
bogdai.summary: A hackathon project exploring a six-agent pipeline for risk analysis on synthetic pharma and healthcare contracts.
bogdai.problem: Contract review needs more than a risk label. A useful finding has to point back to evidence, produce a structured report, and make human review explicit.
bogdai.decision: Separate intake, extraction, grounding, analysis, verification, and reporting. Microsoft Foundry supports grounding against synthetic policies; a deterministic local fallback supports demonstrations without Azure credentials. Pydantic provides report structure.
bogdai.evidence: The project README documents grounded citations, high-risk human-review flags, structured JSON reports, and an agent trace. This portfolio illustration is not running the contract pipeline.
bogdai.limits: Hackathon prototype using synthetic contracts and policies; not legal advice or a validated compliance product. This is a team repository. Sree’s precise individual contribution still needs to be documented.

hasten.name: Hasten Quality
hasten.title: Make ‘ready’ measurable.
hasten.summary: A standalone quality suite for Hasten, a React Native / Expo productivity app.
hasten.problem: Release decisions need observable evidence about behavior, stability, and failure modes. A quality suite can expose gaps that a polished demo does not reveal.
hasten.decision: Combine source-level contract tests with connected-device performance and stress tests. Generate a certification document that records whether release gates pass, with explicit blockers when they do not.
hasten.evidence: The README documents contract, persistence, privacy, state-machine, and device checks. Its recorded run reports engine-quality blockers. Those historical results are not represented here as a current live status.
hasten.limits: Hasten’s documented text engine is rule-based, not AI. This project demonstrates evaluation and delivery engineering. Device checks require a connected device or emulator.
